The SR4 dead_check/uncovered_requirement issue is a genuine evaluation defect, not a mutant defect: mutant gate_trojan_detection_SR4_constant_change_001 adds two documented datapath nodes (the adder's sum bits and carry chain) into suspect_nodes and relabels them from the datapath category to counter/comparator categories -- this is exactly the false-positive mislabeling scenario SR4 exists to catch. Yet evaluate.py still reports fpr=0.00 and PASS on this mutant, per both the validation baseline_run/dead_checks list and the analyzer's per_requirement_coverage (SR4 mutants_detected=0). This shows the false_positive_rate computation in evaluate.py is not counting reported suspect_nodes/stage_labels that overlap with the legitimate documented datapath nodes as false positives -- it is likely only checking for extraneous invented node names rather than mislabeled real nodes, or not cross-referencing stage_labels category correctness at all when computing fpr.
revision_instructions: Rewrite the SR4 false_positive_rate check in evaluate.py (evaluation/evaluate.py) so it actually detects mislabeled legitimate datapath nodes, not just invented/nonexistent node names. The submitted mutant for SR4 adds 'sum_bit' and 'carry' (legitimate documented adder-chain nodes) into suspect_nodes and relabels them in stage_labels from 'datapath' to 'comparator'/'counter' respectively, while still including all true trojan nodes -- this must cause an SR4 FAIL because now 2 of 8 suspect nodes are false positives (fpr=0.25 or higher depending on your normalization), exceeding the pinned threshold. Compute false_positive_rate as: (# nodes in suspect_nodes, or nodes labeled as one of counter/comparator/payload in stage_labels, that are NOT in the hidden ground-truth trigger+payload node set) / (total # nodes reported as suspect/counter/comparator/payload). Do not restrict the false-positive check to only catch invented net names -- it must also flag legitimate real nets (present in netlist.v, part of the documented datapath) that get mislabeled into a trojan category. After the fix, confirm: golden submission (which correctly labels sum_bit/carry as 'datapath') still PASSES SR4 with fpr=0.00, and the SR4 mutant (which relabels those same nodes into counter/comparator) now FAILS SR4.
